Design a solid circular shaft diameter based solely on the angle-of-twist (stiffness) limit.
The shaft is solid, circular, and analyzed under small-deformation, linear-elastic assumptions.
The applied torque is T = 1,000,000 N·mm (1000 N·m).
The shaft length is L = 1500 mm.
The shaft material is 6061-T6 aluminum with shear modulus G = 25939.8 MPa.
The allowable angle of twist over the full length is φ_allow = 0.75°, which must be converted to φ_allow = 0.01309 rad for use in the twist equation.
Work entirely in the N–mm–MPa unit system.
Use the governing relation φ = TL/(JG) with the polar moment of inertia J = πd⁴/32 for a solid circular cross-section.
Solve for the minimum diameter d such that φ = TL/(JG) ≤ φ_allow = 0.01309 rad over L = 1500 mm.
The design diameter is governed only by the stiffness (twist) criterion; strength is not part of the requirement.
Present the governing relations clearly, showing the derivation of d from φ = TL/(JG) with J = πd⁴/32.
State all assumptions used, including linear-elastic behavior, uniform circular cross-section, constant torque along the length, and rigid end conditions.
As an optional supplementary note only (not part of the governing design criterion), report the maximum torsional shear stress τ = Tc/J at the designed diameter; this check does not alter the design diameter.
Report the final minimum required shaft diameter in mm based on the twist limit.
